title: Integral mapping-limit comparison and its actual projections
statement:
Fix $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$ of characteristic $p$, a prime $\ell\ne p$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, its valuation ring $R$, a uniformizer $\varpi$, and $A_n=R/\varpi^n$ for $n\ge1$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber, def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. On the small pro-etale site of a scheme $W$ put $B_{n,W}=(A_n)_W$ and $R_W=\lim_nB_{n,W}$ [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients]. Use ordinary derived categories of module sheaves and the Roos-complete constructible category $D^b_c(W,R)$, whose finite reductions are constructible with a common bounded cohomological support [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed, def-weil-derived-complete]. Write $P_n=P\otimes^L_{R_W}B_{n,W}$ [def-weil-integral-derived-reduction]. Use the strict semilinear coefficient-system category $\mathscr S_W$, the adjunction $\mathcal R_W\dashv\mathcal L_W$, its actual unit $u$ and counit $e$, and the mapping systems $\mathcal H_W$ of [lem-coef-derived-system-evaluation-calculus]; here $\mathcal R_WP=(P_n)_n$ with its coherent quotient maps and $\mathcal L_W=R\lim\operatorname{Res}$.

Let $W$ be a separated finite-type $k$-scheme [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties] and $P,Q\in D^b_c(W,R)$. Write $R\operatorname{Hom}_{W,R}(P,Q)=R\Gamma(W_{\mathrm{proet}},R\mathcal Hom_{R_W}(P,Q))$ for the global derived mapping complex [def-pur-derived-internal-hom, lem-pur-rhom-global-sections]. Set $N=\mathcal R_WQ$, and let $\gamma$ be the specified enriched reduction/limit adjunction of the system calculus. The composite
$$\lambda_{P,Q}=\gamma_{P,N}\circ R\operatorname{Hom}_{W,R}(P,u_Q):R\operatorname{Hom}_{W,R}(P,Q)\xrightarrow{\sim}R\lim\mathcal H_W(\mathcal R_WP,\mathcal R_WQ)$$
is a natural isomorphism in $D(\operatorname{Ab})$, compatible with shifts and composition of mapping complexes. Its composite with each actual mapping-limit projection is the map induced by $Q\to\operatorname{Res}_nQ_n$, followed by the derived scalar-extension/restriction adjunction [lem-weil-derived-scalar-extension-restriction-adjunction]. On degree-zero Hom this sends $h:P\to Q$ to
$$e_{\mathcal R_WQ,n}\circ(u_Q)_n\circ h_n=h_n.$$
For every integer $r$ the corresponding map on shifted Hom sends $h:P\to Q[r]$ to $h_n:P_n\to Q_n[r]$. Thus the projections are reduction of the actual integral morphisms. Only the first input is extended in the scalar adjunction and the second is restricted; the assertion contains no tensor/base-change assertion for an integral internal Hom.

proof.text: By [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed], $Q$ is derived complete in the stated Roos sense. Apply [lem-pur-normalized-actual-reconstruction-maps] on $W$: $N=\mathcal R_WQ$ is normalized and the actual unit $u_Q:Q\to\mathcal L_WN$ is invertible. Its hypotheses hold since $\ell\ne p$ is invertible on a $k$-scheme. This uses the theorem about the actual unit, not uniqueness of a lift of the finite reduction maps. In Lean the intrinsic completeness predicate of the constructible category is first identified with legacy Roos completeness by lem-sf-derived-complete-legacy-comparison. An auxiliary universe-zero finite field of characteristic different from l supplies only the erased bookkeeping datum of IntegralOnSlice.IsComplete. The actual characteristic of the given base field proves l invertible on X by the map on global sections.

proof.text: Apply the specified $\gamma_{P,N}$ of [lem-coef-derived-system-evaluation-calculus] to the normalized $N$ from step 1. Functoriality of derived Hom sends $u_Q$ and its inverse to inverse maps. Thus $\gamma_{P,N}\circ R\operatorname{Hom}(P,u_Q)$ is precisely the asserted isomorphism $\lambda_{P,Q}$ in $D(\operatorname{Ab})$. Naturality follows from naturality of $u$ and $\gamma$. For a composable pair with middle object $Q$ and target $T$, the equation $u_Tg=(\mathcal L_W\mathcal R_Wg)u_Q$ and the calculus's composition and unit compatibilities identify composition after $\lambda$ with composition of the reduced mapping systems; these are identities of mapping complexes, before taking finite projections. For the internal composition clause, rewrite RHom(P,u_Q) followed by the enriched adjunct as the adjoint of beta(P,Q); tensoring these adjoints and composing with the lax counit mate is the adjunct of tensoring their original maps. The calculus beta composition equation then proves the square.

proof.text: The calculus's projection formula says the $n$th projection after $\gamma$ is $(\pi_n)_*$ followed by scalar adjunction. Precomposing with $R\operatorname{Hom}(P,u_Q)$ replaces $\pi_n$ by $\pi_nu_Q$, which is the actual reduction unit $Q\to\operatorname{Res}_nQ_n$ by the same cited statement. On degree-zero Hom its formula gives $e_{N,n}(u_Q)_nh_n$. Evaluate the adjunction triangle identity $e_{\mathcal R_WQ}\,\mathcal R_W(u_Q)=1_{\mathcal R_WQ}$ at $n$ to obtain $e_{N,n}(u_Q)_nh_n=h_n$. This computes the specified projections without identifying maps into a derived limit by their projections. Naturality of the fixed coefficientHomZeroEquiv interprets this equality on H-zero, for arbitrary ambient P,Q. This stronger ambient formula directly handles shifted Hom without requiring Q[r] to carry a constructible-category structure.

proof.text: Apply lem-coef-enriched-global-shift to the underlying ambient P and Q. Its comparison, source shift and target shift are definitionally the three unchanged mapping-limit maps of this module, so it proves exactly the mapping-complex shift clause. The all-integer shifted-Hom formula follows independently from the ambient H-zero calculation of step 3. The separate shift lemma contains no isomorphism, projection, H-zero, triangle or composition assertion. No finite projection detection is used.
